scope: Crossed registry x presentation x model-pair test. Identifies the presentation effect within a registry (reviewer M4) and places the fidelity of a contemporary strong pair on the same scale as the weak pairs (reviewer M11).

preregistration.primary_endpoint: fidelity_joint_profile (fraction of committed steps on which BOTH roles play the Eq.(1) target profile)
preregistration.note_on_fidelity_definition: The paper currently reports 4.1% (joint profile) and 0.28 (per-role) as if they were the same quantity (reviewer M3). P10 reports both for every cell, with the denominator stated, and the decision rules read the joint-profile definition only.

rationale.registries: R_rq3_* is RQ3's own registry, R_rq5_* is RQ5's. Each pooled registry keeps the original 4 matrices per family bit-exact and adds 20 fresh draws from the identical sampler, so G = 24 per family, meeting supplement D's own confirmatory threshold that Table 2 (G = 4) failed.
rationale.presentations: Advisory is the archived GatedBaseline cue; RoleBound is the presentation P7D froze. No third presentation is introduced.
rationale.relabel_mode: In anti_safe and anti_tradeoff the Eq.(1) target is always the (A,B) cell, so a positional bias would sit inside the primary endpoint. Balanced relabelling moves the target through all four cells across the four seeds of every matrix.

sampling.note: warmup_episodes x horizon = 40 steps, exactly the min_total_observations the action certificate requires; the warm-up block is shared by every arm in a cell (common random numbers).

pilot.note: max_tokens is a harness parameter, not a treatment. It is frozen per role by the pilot on a coordination-family probe matrix that no analysed family contains, before the campaign starts; the pilot never enters the analysis.

pairs.label: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 x Phi-3.5-mini-instruct (the RQ3/RQ5 pair)
pairs.why: The reference pair. Re-running it under this one harness is what makes the M4 contrast an experiment rather than a comparison of two campaigns that differed in runner, max_tokens and episode split as well as in registry and presentation.

pairs.label: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct x GLM-4-9B-0414 (the source pair)
pairs.why: Optional middle rung of the capability ladder. Local weights, so it costs GPU time but no quota.

pairs.label: gpt-oss-120b x qwen3-32b, both on a free hosted endpoint
pairs.why: The fast free lane: both roles sit on the same free tier with independent per-model daily quotas, so the two roles do not contend and the whole campaign runs unattended without a GPU. Both are open weights, so the reproducibility claim survives: a reviewer re-serves the pinned revisions with vLLM and re-runs offline.

pairs.label: gpt-oss-120b (Groq) x GLM-4.7 (Cerebras)
pairs.why: The most contemporary free pair, and cross-vendor like the paper's other pairs. Slower lane: the Cerebras free tier is token-per-day bound, so budget roughly 3.8k requests/day on that role.

pairs.label: Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B x HY3-295B, both free on an aggregator
pairs.why: The largest free-tier models, for a top rung of the ladder. Most quota-constrained: 20 rpm and a daily cap that only lifts after a one-off credit purchase, so treat this as a screening-tier pair only.

models_snapshot.warning: Free-tier catalogues and quotas move. Run `python reproduce/p10_check_access.py --protocol protocols/p10_factorial_frozen.json` first: it reports which configured models the key can actually reach, what the provider says the limits are, and resolves each hf_repo to a commit hash. The runner refuses to start until every hf_revision is a real hash, because a hosted endpoint that cannot be re-served offline would cost the paper its reproducibility claim.
models_snapshot.requirement: Strong pairs MUST be open weights. Closed frontier APIs are rejected by p10_backend on purpose.

success_requires: positional_bias.max_minus_min_across_target_cells <= 0.15 for every analysed pair and arm
analysis.reporting_commitment: Every verdict this file can emit -- including REGISTRY_EXPLAINS and CAPABILITY_ACCOUNT, both of which force the paper to withdraw or narrow its second contribution -- is written into the protocol before the run, with the exact paper edit it implies. A null or unfavourable outcome is reportable as-is.
